stem: A 7-month-old infant in an Australian emergency department has an acute upper-airway illness, and when placed supine their neck flexes; which anatomical feature best explains why airway positioning is an immediate priority?
explanation: Large occiput. In infants, a proportionally large occiput can flex the neck when the child lies flat, so airway positioning becomes an immediate priority during upper-airway assessment.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Respiratory 3.1 Acute Respiratory Problems

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because a smaller airway diameter increases resistance, but it does not explain the neck flexion seen when the infant is laid flat.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because a longer, floppier epiglottis is a paediatric airway feature, but it is not the reason supine positioning causes neck flexion.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because a large tongue can contribute to airway obstruction, but the feature specifically linked to lying-flat neck flexion is the large occiput.
optionExplanations.D: Correct because infants have a proportionally large occiput, which can flex the neck when lying supine and makes airway positioning an immediate priority.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because fewer alveoli relate to gas exchange, not to neck flexion from supine positioning.
